mainTopic: The four shavings of a נזיר who is a מצורע are a מצוה; a new chapter on who can become a נזיר (גוים, women, slaves) and the sources for it
overview: The amud opens with רבי חייא's ברייתא. It teaches that a מצורע's shaving cannot count as a נזיר's shaving, because the two happen at opposite times: before or after immersion, and before or after the blood is sprinkled. Next, רמי בר חמא asks whether the משנה's four shavings are a מצוה, or only a way to clear away hair that grew in טומאה. The practical difference is whether a hair-removing paste (נשא) would work. רבא proves they are a מצוה, because if the goal were only hair removal, three shavings would be enough. The chapter שני נזירים ends, and a new משנה teaches that גוים cannot become נזירים, while women and slaves can. The משנה adds that a master can force his slave to break his נזירות, but a husband cannot force his wife. The גמרא finds the sources in a ברייתא: 'בני ישראל' leaves out גוים, and 'ואמרת אליהם' includes slaves. רבא explains that the extra words for slaves are needed because slaves are normally left out of vows. The גמרא then challenges the source for leaving out גוים, using the example of ערכין. It turns to the פסוק 'לאביו ולאמו לא יטמא' and tests what that פסוק teaches, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The shavings of a leper and a nazirite happen at different times
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that a מצורע's shaving and a נזיר's shaving are different, so one cannot count for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא teaches: this one (the מצורע) shaves before going into the water, and that one (the impure נזיר) shaves after going into the water. This one (the מצורע) shaves before the blood is sprinkled, and that one (the pure נזיר) shaves after the blood is sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from רבי חייא that supports the rule that a מצורע's shaving cannot do double duty as a נזיר's shaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא lists two differences in timing. A מצורע shaves before immersing, but an impure נזיר shaves after immersing. A מצורע also shaves before his offering's blood is sprinkled, but a pure נזיר shaves after his offering's blood is sprinkled. Since the shavings belong at opposite points in each process, they are separate acts and one cannot cover both.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches (introduces a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה)
Literally 'entering the water', meaning immersion in a מקוה
Sprinkling of the blood of an offering on the מזבח
A person with the skin affliction צרעת

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya teaches:
This one is before immersion in (living) water
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the מצורע. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, 'living'.

phrases.english: and that one is after immersion in water;
this one is before the sprinkling of the blood
and that one is after the sprinkling of the blood.
phrases.notes: Here 'that one' is the pure נזיר finishing his נזירות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the earlier rule (on the previous page) that a leper's shaving does not count for a nazirite's shaving.
steps.raayaObject: That a מצורע's shaving cannot count as a נזיר's shaving.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי חייא showing that the two shavings have opposite timing, both relative to immersion and relative to the blood being sprinkled.

steps.title: Are the four shavings a מצוה or just hair removal?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks why the נזיר in the משנה shaves four times: is each shaving a מצוה, or is it only to get rid of hair that grew in טומאה?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'that the shaving of the leprosy...' רמי בר חמא asked: these four shavings the משנה talks about, are they done because shaving is a מצוה, or only to get rid of hair that grew while he was impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line of the משנה about the four shavings. רמי בר חמא asks what the reason for them is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to understand the shavings. Either the act of shaving itself is the מצוה, or the real goal is simply to clear away hair that grew in טומאה so that new, pure hair can grow. רמי בר חמא wants to know which one it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks, raising a question that needs to be settled
Shavings (plural of תִּגְלַחַת)
To remove / to get rid of
Hair that grew during the time of impurity

phrases.english: "That the shaving of the leprosy," etc.
Rami bar Chama asked:
These four shavings that it mentions,
are they because of a מצוה,
or in order to remove hair of impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the משנה's four shavings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the reason for the four shavings the מצוה of shaving, or the removal of hair grown in טומאה?

steps.title: What practical difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons.
steps.whatsHappening: Before trying to answer רמי בר חמא, the גמרא asks why his question matters in practice. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to make sure the question has a real halachic result. Otherwise it would only be a question about the reason, with no change in what a person actually does.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference?

phrases.english: What difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of רמי בר חמא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical halachic outcome depends on whether the shavings are a מצוה or just hair removal?

steps.title: The difference: using a hair-removing paste
steps.stepSummary: If the shavings are a מצוה, a hair-removing paste does not work. If they are only to remove impure hair, a paste works too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is whether he may remove the hair with a hair-removing paste. If you say it is because of a מצוה, removing it with a paste is not enough. But if you say it is only to remove impure hair, then even if he smeared on a paste, that also works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is whether a hair-removing paste (נשא) can be used instead of a razor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מצוה is the act of shaving, then only real shaving counts, and a paste would not fulfill it. If the only goal is to get the impure hair off, then it does not matter how it comes off, so a paste would be fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A hair-removing paste (depilatory)
He smeared it on
If you say

phrases.english: For removing it with a depilatory.
If you say it is because of a מצוה,
removing with a depilatory is not acceptable,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מִשּׁוּם אַעְבּוֹרֵי שְׂעַר טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: but if you say it is to remove hair of impurity,
even if he smeared on a depilatory, that also works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what practical difference there is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether a hair-removing paste is acceptable: it is not acceptable if the shavings are a מצוה, but it is acceptable if they are only to remove impure hair.

steps.title: רבא's proof: three shavings would be enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא that says 'four shavings', and argues that if hair removal were the only goal, three would be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the answer? רבא said: come and hear a source that says, 'And he shaves four shavings.' If you think the shavings are only to remove impure hair, then even three should be enough for him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to settle רמי בר חמא's question using a ברייתא that counts four shavings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only goal were getting rid of impure hair, one of the four shavings would be extra, because the other shavings already take the hair off. The fact that the ברייתא still requires four shows that each shaving has its own purpose. That points to each one being a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof from a source)
If it would enter your mind (introduces an assumption that will be rejected)
It would be enough for him

phrases.english: What is the answer?
Rava said: Come and hear:
"And he shaves four shavings."
If it would enter your mind
that it is to remove hair of impurity,
even three would also be enough for him!
phrases.notes: The shaving that is only there to clear impure hair would be extra, since the other shavings already take the hair off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to settle רמי בר חמא's question.
steps.raayaObject: That the four shavings are done as a מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that requires four shavings, while the hair-removal reason would only need three.

steps.title: Conclusion: the shavings are a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the four shavings are a מצוה, so a hair-removing paste would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that the shavings are because of a מצוה. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws his conclusion, and the גמרא agrees: the shavings are a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since four shavings are required even though three would remove all the impure hair, the shaving itself must be the מצוה. In practice, that means real shaving is needed and a hair-removing paste would not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this / that settles it

steps.whatToRemember: The four shavings are a מצוה, not just a way to clear impure hair. So they must be done by actually shaving, and a hair-removing paste does not work.

phrases.english: Learn from this that it is because of a מצוה.
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבא's proof and closes the question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The four shavings are required as a מצוה, so a hair-removing paste does not fulfill them.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of שני נזירים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the פרק called שני נזירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'Two Nazirites.'
steps.whatsHappening: The previous chapter is finished. This line closes it before a new chapter begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הדרן עלך' is a traditional farewell to a finished chapter. It contains no new הלכה. It only marks a boundary in the text.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the closing formula at the end of a פרק
'Two Nazirites': the name of the chapter that just ended

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Two Nazirites'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose discussion ended in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter שני נזירים is complete.

steps.title: New משנה: who can become a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: גוים cannot become a נזיר, but נשים and עבדים can. A master can force his slave to break the נזירות, but a husband cannot force his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Non-Jews do not have נזירות. Women and slaves do have נזירות. Women are stricter than slaves, because a master can force his slave to break his נזירות, but a husband cannot force his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה listing who can and cannot take on נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes three points. First, גוים are not part of נזירות at all. Second, women and slaves are. Third, among those two, a woman's נזירות is firmer, because her husband cannot override it, while a master can override his slave's.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-Jews
The state of being a נזיר (no wine, no haircuts, no contact with the dead)
Canaanite slaves owned by a Jew
A stricter side, a stringency
Forces

phrases.english: Non-Jews do not have נזירות.
Women and slaves do have נזירות.
There is a stricter side to women than to slaves,
since he (the master) can force his slave,
phrases.notes: He can force the slave to act against his נזירות, for example to drink wine.

phrases.english: but he (a husband) cannot force his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גוים have no נזירות. נשים and עבדים do. A master can force his slave to break it, but a husband cannot force his wife.

steps.title: Asking for the source that גוים have no נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's first rule and asks where it comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches: non-Jews do not have נזירות. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks for its source in the תורה. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple request for a source, not a challenge. The answer will also explain the משנה's second rule, about slaves.

keyTerms.meaning: It (the משנה) teaches
'From where are these words?': where is the source for this?

phrases.english: גמרא: It teaches:
Non-Jews do not have נזירות.
From where are these things learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's first rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The תורה source showing that גוים cannot become a נזיר.

steps.title: The ברייתא: 'בני ישראל' leaves out גוים, 'אליהם' includes עבדים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'Speak to the children of Israel' as leaving out גוים, and 'and say to them' as including slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'Speak to the children of Israel' means not to non-Jews. 'And say to them' comes to include slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads two parts of the נזיר פסוק. One part leaves out גוים, and the other adds slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בני ישראל' limit נזירות to Jews, which explains the משנה's first rule. The extra words 'ואמרת אליהם' widen the law to include slaves, which explains part of the second rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught: introduces a ברייתא
To include, to add to the law

phrases.english: As the רבנן taught:
'Speak to the children of Israel', and not to non-Jews.
'And say to them' comes to include slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בני ישראל' leaves out גוים, and 'ואמרת אליהם' includes עבדים.

steps.title: Why is a פסוק needed to include slaves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's need to include slaves, since slaves are normally obligated in every מצוה women are obligated in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a פסוק? Didn't you say: any מצוה a woman is obligated in, a slave is obligated in too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second half of the ברייתא. Since women can be נזירים, slaves should be included automatically, without any extra פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a slave's obligations match a woman's. The פסוק already includes women as נזירים ('איש או אשה'). So the extra words 'ואמרת אליהם' seem to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need a פסוק?': the teaching seems unnecessary
But you (we) have said
Obligated

phrases.english: Why do I need a פסוק?
Didn't you say:
any מצוה that a woman is obligated in,
a slave is obligated in it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second teaching of the ברייתא from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'ואמרת אליהם' to include slaves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule that a slave matches a woman in מצוות already makes slaves נזירים, so the extra פסוק seems pointless.

steps.title: רבא: slaves are left out of vows, so we needed the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that a slave is excluded from vows because he does not own himself. Without the פסוק, we would have thought he is excluded from נזירות as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Here it is different, because the פסוק says 'to bind a bond on his soul', meaning one whose self belongs to him. A slave is left out, since his self does not belong to him. Since his self does not belong to him, you might say he cannot become a נזיר either. So the פסוק teaches us that he can.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. Vows are a special area where slaves are left out, so the usual 'slave equals woman' rule might have failed here. That is why the פסוק has to include slaves in נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'whatever a woman is obligated in, so is a slave' does not apply to vows. The פסוק of נדרים limits vows to someone who owns himself, and a slave belongs to his master. Since נזירות is a kind of vow, we would have excluded slaves from it, and 'ואמרת אליהם' tells us they are included.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different
His self is owned by him: he is his own master
Since
I might say: introduces a mistaken assumption
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: A slave cannot make ordinary נדרים because he does not own himself. The extra words 'ואמרת אליהם' still make him able to become a נזיר.
steps.confusionAlert: The verse 'לאסר אסר על נפשו' is not the source that includes slaves in נזירות. It is the reason we would have excluded them. The word 'אליהם' is what includes them.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Here it is different,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the area of vows, which includes נזירות.

phrases.english: since the פסוק says 'to bind a bond on his soul',
meaning one whose self belongs to him.

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא עֶבֶד, שֶׁאֵין נַפְשׁוֹ קְנוּיָה לוֹ.
phrases.english: This leaves out a slave, whose self does not belong to him.
Since his self does not belong to him,
you might say that with נזיר too he cannot.
So it (the פסוק) teaches us otherwise.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the general rule would have failed here, so the פסוק is needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since slaves are left out of vows, they would be left out of נזירות too, despite the rule linking them to women.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ואמרת אליהם' is needed to teach that a slave can become a נזיר.

steps.title: Does the word 'Israel' always leave out gentiles? The case of valuations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that 'בני ישראל' leaves out גוים. It points out that by ערכין the same words leave out גוים in only one way, while the word 'איש' includes them in another way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: 'Speak to the children of Israel', and not to gentiles. But does every place that says 'Israel' leave out gentiles? By valuations it also says 'Speak to the children of Israel', and a ברייתא teaches: Jews can pledge a valuation, but gentiles cannot. You might think gentiles also cannot be valued, so the verse says 'a man' to include them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא from step 10 again and attacks it. In ערכין, the words 'בני ישראל' do not fully leave גוים out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By ערכין, 'בני ישראל' only stops a גוי from making the pledge, while the word 'איש' still lets a גוי be the one who is valued. The פסוק of נזיר also says 'איש'. So maybe a גוי should be included in נזירות too, and 'בני ישראל' alone is not a strong enough source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The master said', the formula for quoting an earlier teaching in order to discuss it
Valuation pledges: promising to give the Temple the Torah's set value of a person
They can make a valuation pledge (be the one who pledges)
They can be valued (be the person whose value is pledged)
'The verse teaches', introducing a פסוק used as proof

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מעריכין and נערכין. מעריכין means making the pledge. נערכין means being the person whose value is pledged. A גוי cannot do the first but can be the second.

phrases.english: The master said:
phrases.notes: He is quoting the ברייתא from step 10.

phrases.english: "Speak to the children of Israel", and not to gentiles.
And wherever "Israel" is written,
are gentiles not included?
But regarding valuations,
where it is written "Speak to the children of Israel",
and a ברייתא taught:
The children of Israel can pledge a valuation,
but gentiles cannot pledge a valuation.
One might think they cannot be valued either,
so the verse says: "a man".
phrases.notes: The same word 'איש' also opens the פסוק of נזיר, and that is the problem being raised.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיב ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״, גּוֹיִם לָא? וְהָא גַּבֵּי עֲרָכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first half of the ברייתא from step 10 (the part about גוים) and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading that 'בני ישראל' leaves גוים out of נזירות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By ערכין, 'בני ישראל' does not fully leave out גוים, because 'איש' includes them as people who can be valued. נזיר also says 'איש', so גוים might be included there too.

steps.title: A different source: 'For his father and mother he shall not become impure'
steps.stepSummary: נזיר is different, because its פסוק speaks about one who has a father, and a גוי is considered to have no father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because the verse says: 'For his father and his mother he shall not become impure.' This applies to one who has a father. That leaves out a gentile, who has no father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that נזיר has its own special פסוק that leaves out גוים, so it is not like ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'איש' may include גוים, but the later פסוק about a נזיר not becoming טמא for his father shows the law is for someone who 'has a father.' A גוי is described as having no father, so he is left out. What exactly 'no father' means is the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here it is different', a formula that separates one case from another
He shall not become ritually impure
'Goes out', meaning this case is left out

phrases.english: Here it is different,
because the verse says:
"For his father and for his mother he shall not become impure",
so it applies to one who has a father,
which leaves out a gentile, who has no father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ערכין challenge by bringing a different פסוק for נזיר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a new פסוק that applies only to נזיר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of 'איש', a גוי might be able to become a נזיר just as he can be valued
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לאביו ולאמו' limits נזירות to one who 'has a father', and that leaves out a גוי

steps.title: In what way does a gentile have no father?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what it means that a גוי 'has no father'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding what [does he have no father]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear meaning of 'has no father.' This sets up the next few steps, which test possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי obviously has a biological father, so 'no father' must mean that in some legal sense his father does not count. The גמרא wants to know in which sense.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For what?' or 'regarding what?', asking for the exact meaning

phrases.english: Regarding what?
phrases.notes: In what way is a גוי considered to have no father?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the answer in step 14 means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what legal sense a גוי 'has no father'

steps.title: Not inheritance: a gentile does inherit his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'no father' refers to inheritance. It rejects this because רבי יוחנן teaches that a גוי inherits his father by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about inheritance, did רבי חייא בר אבין not say in the name of רבי יוחנן that a gentile inherits his father by Torah law? As it says: 'For I have given Mount Seir to עשו as an inheritance'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first answer, inheritance, and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גוי could not inherit his father, it would make sense to say his father doesn't count for him. But רבי יוחנן proves from עשו inheriting הר שעיר that a גוי does inherit by Torah law. So inheritance cannot be the meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say', introducing a suggestion that will be rejected
Inheritance
By Torah law
Mount Seir, the land given to עשו

phrases.english: If you say it is regarding inheritance,
but did not Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אָבִיו דְּבַר תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: A gentile inherits his father by Torah law,
as it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי יְרֻשָּׁה לְעֵשָׂו נָתַתִּי אֶת הַר שֵׂעִיר״!
phrases.english: "For I have given Mount Seir to Esav as an inheritance"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא לְעִנְיַן יְרוּשָּׁה, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 15 and rejects it
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'no father' means a גוי cannot inherit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן proves that a גוי inherits his father by Torah law, so he does 'have a father' when it comes to inheritance

steps.title: Perhaps it means a gentile is not commanded to honor his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's new suggestion is that 'having a father' means being commanded to honor him, and a גוי is not commanded in this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it applies to one who is commanded about honoring his father.
steps.whatsHappening: Since inheritance did not work, the גמרא offers a second meaning for 'has a father.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'having a father' means having the מצוה of כיבוד אב. A גוי is not given that commandment, so legally it is as if he has no father, and he is left out of נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather', bringing a new explanation after the last one failed
Commanded or warned about something
The מצוה of honoring one's father

phrases.english: Rather, it applies to one who is commanded
about honoring his father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁמּוּזְהָר עַל כִּיבּוּד אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected inheritance explanation with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new meaning to 'has a father'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Has a father' meant inheritance, which does not work
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Has a father' means one who is commanded to honor his father

steps.title: But honoring parents is not mentioned by נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the honoring-parents explanation because the פסוקים about נזיר say nothing about honoring one's father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is 'Honor your father' written in the section about a נזיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the second explanation. Honoring parents has nothing to do with the topic of נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of נזיר speaks about not becoming טמא for a father, not about honoring him. Bringing in the מצוה of כיבוד אב adds an idea the פסוק never mentions, so the explanation fails.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it written?', a challenge saying a source does not say what is claimed
Regarding, in the section about

phrases.english: Is "Honor your father" written
in the section about a נזיר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges and rejects the explanation in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'has a father' means being commanded to honor one's father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נזיר section does not mention honoring parents, so that idea cannot be read into the פסוק

steps.title: A new reading: the verse is about one who can become impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'has a father' approach. It reads the same פסוק as speaking about one who 'has טומאה', meaning one who can become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse says: 'For his father and his mother he shall not become impure.' This applies to one who has impurity...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the same פסוק but changes what it learns from it. The focus is now on the word 'impure' instead of the word 'father.' The sentence continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father explanations failed, so the גמרא now uses the word 'יטמא'. The law of נזיר is for someone to whom טומאה applies. The text here stops after 'one who has טומאה', and the rest of the thought continues next.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity
'The verse says', bringing a פסוק as the source

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says:
"For his father and for his mother he shall not become impure",
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:7, the same פסוק as step 14, now read with a different focus.

phrases.english: so it applies to one who has impurity,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אָמַר קְרָא ״לְאָבִיו וּלְאִמּוֹ לֹא יִטַּמָּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both 'father' explanations failed, reads the same פסוק in a new way
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the same פסוק with the focus on 'יטמא' instead of 'אביו'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exclusion of a גוי came from his 'having no father', which could not be explained
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק speaks of one who has טומאה; the rest of the thought continues on the next part of the daf
